Regarding minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring for acute myeloid leukemia (AML), which statement(s) is(are) true ?
(1) MRD after consolidation chemotherapy may has a better prognosis prediction than MRD after induction chemotherapy.
(2) Multiparameter flow cytometry is often used for MRD measurement.
(3) Patients with negative MRD before transplantation had lower relapse rate comparing to those with positive MRD.
(4) As a MRD marker, TET2 offers better predicting value comparing to RUNX1-RUNX1T1 rearrangement
ebmt_chapters: Ch57 Monitoring Measurable Residual Disease in ALL and AML (PDF p516–524)

A study of 2941 recipients of allo-HSCT in Seattle confirmed the importance of several risk factors in predicting the occurrence of moderate to severe aGvHD. In contrast they also found that some previous known factors did not impact on the likelihood of aGvHD, but were associated with the occurrence of cGvHD. (Flowers et al. 2011) According to their findings, which of the following factors did not impact on the likelihood of acute GvHD?
(1) Increasing donor age.
(2) The use of female donors for male recipients.
(3) Cytokine-mobilized stem cells.
(4) The administration of high-dose TBI.
ebmt_chapters: Ch12 Donor Selection for Adults and Pediatrics (PDF p143–155)

Currently available treatment modality for prevention of post-allo-HSCT relapse in an AML CR2 patient with high alles burden of FLT-3/ITD mutation including:
(1) Administration of 2nd generation of FLT3 inhibitors immediately after engraftment
(2) Administration of hypomethylation agent immediately after engraftment
(3) Taper immunosuppressants as soon as possible
(4) Donor leukocyte infusion in a fixed schedule
ebmt_chapters: Ch58 Prevention and Treatment of Relapse by Drugs (PDF p525–531)

Bacterial infections occurring during late phase of HSCT are general secondary to:
(1) encapsulated bacteria
(2) chronic GvHD
(3) treatment of chronic GvHD
(4) functional asplenia
(5) hypogammaglobulinemia

Which of the following statements in regarding to patients with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) receiving allogeneic HSCT is CORRECT?
(1) Patients with primary myelofibrosis have relative lower rate (<15%) of engraftment failure after allo-HSCT.
(2) In a retrospective single center experience, no achievement of molecular remission on day 180 post-allograft was associated with a significant higher incidence of a subsequent clinical relapse.
(3) Due to a lack of graft-versus-myelofibrosis effect, donor lymphocyte infusion has not been successfully applied in patients with residual disease to induce a molecular remission
(4) Once leukemic transformation occurs, the probability of a successful HSCT declines significantly to about half of what is achievable with earlier HSCT.
ebmt_chapters: Ch59 Delayed Transfer of Immune Cells or the Art of Donor Lymphocyte Infusion (DLI) 2.0 (PDF p532–540)

stem:
Which of the following statements of treatment for multiple myeloma is (are) correct?
(1) Induction therapy with thalidomide/dexamethasone or bortezomib/dexamethasone produces 10% complete remission (CR) in first line situation.
(2) Induction therapy with bortezomib-based triplets like PAD or VCD is inferior to combination of bortezomib plus lenalidomide.
(3) Autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) after induction therapy will add 15-20% more CR rate.
(4) With the available navel agents (carfilzomib or daratumumab), autologous HSCT in front line is no more a standard therapy for fit patients.

The following statements describe use of G-CSF in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Please select all the CORRECT answer(s).
(1) G-CSF use is recommended after autologous HCT
(2) G-CSF use is NOT routinely recommended after allogeneic HCT
(3) G-CSF is used for PB stem cell mobilization based on its direct stimulatory effect on bone marrow stem cells.
(4) Retrospective studies show increased risk of GVHD after G-CSF use in allogeneic HSCT
(5) G-CSF use provides obvious survival benefit.
ebmt_chapters: Ch16 Mobilization and Collection of HSC (PDF p180–186)

stem:
The facts about respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) include:
(1) RSV is an RNA virus
(2) Winter season is a risk factor for acquisition of RSV in HCT recipients
(3) About 20-50% of patients with RSV URI progress to pneumonia.
(4) Low dose steroid appears to have significant impact on progression to pneumonia
(5) Ribavirin often is ineffective to control the RSV disease.

Which of the following statements in regarding to myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) are CORRECT?
(1) Delayed allo-HSCT is associated with reduced chances of prolonged relapse-free survival.
(2) Patients with less advanced MDS categories may benefit from deferred allo-HSCT after they develop poor-risk features.
(3) Allo-HSCT outcomes have improved progressively in recent years, mainly due to a gradual reduction in posttransplant relapse.
(4) A number of questions remain to be resolved by prospective studies, such as the choice of donor, including haplo-identical donors, the role of osttransplant treatment, and the timing of transplantation in patients with lower risk MDS.
